A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DeepLIFT is an efficient and stable way of approximating the influence of each neuron to the output of a neural network.
DeepLIFT can explain how the input is affected by every parameter in the network, and can thus serve as a tool for feature selection, and aiding model debugging.
DeepLIFT is the first method to provide a generic approach for computing contributions to a “black-box” machine learning model without relying on interpolation techniques in the input space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DeepLIFT framework provides a way for us to understand how the network makes its predictions, and can be used to identify the features which contribute to a prediction.
the DeepLIFT algorithm is able to identify features that are relevant for the model’s prediction, and can do so without any additional training.
we have shown a way to interpret neural networks by decomposing the contribution of each feature to the output.
